entries.subject: DAMIT 3920: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-3920.txt. Model 3920, version 2019-05-07, pole (272°, 22°), period 21.2689 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: NEOWISE Gr12b: selected thermal size
entries.finding: The original IRSA query was rerun for asteroid 5436; its Gr12b row matches the retained diameter 37.6960 km, error 0.3290 km, fit code DVB- and mean epoch 2455205.1770080. D in FIT_CODE means diameter was fitted. This effective-sphere diameter provides an approximate display scale, not a resolved surface or an independent physical-volume fit to the shape.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: The grid marks unmapped coverage: no registered global reflectance mosaic was found in the selected releases. Convex inversion leaves concavities and fine relief unresolved. - Transferring thermal diameter to mesh volume is approximate. The quoted fit error excludes additional thermal/shape uncertainty and does not measure local shape accuracy. - Elevation is false color for model radius minus a reference sphere, not gravitational height or independent terrain. - Absolute phase is arbitrary; accelerated display spin is illustrative. Orbit context is fixed at 2026-09-03 TT. The archive also lists an alternative pole. - The selected sidereal period is 21.2689 h; [SBDB](https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api?sstr=5436&phys-par=true) repeats French et al. (2013)’s older 38.41 h synodic value. The selected shape and sidereal spin remain paired. The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 3921: pole (96°, 11°), 21.269 h, version 2019-05-07. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: Source mesh and calibration preservation
entries.finding: The [original mesh](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/stored_files/open/12274/shape.txt) is retained without changing its coordinates or connectivity. [DAMIT documentation](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/pages/documentation) supplies the coordinate units, pole and sidereal-period conventions; its CC BY 4.0 terms and other credits are linked from NOTICE.md.

entries.subject: Hanuš 2023: consistency with the existing DAMIT solution
entries.finding: The existing-DAMIT table was checked: (272°, 22°), 21.2689 h, agreeing with the selected archive solution to the paper’s printed precision. Included as a source consistency check, not a newly adopted mesh or surface qualification.

entries.subject: Alternative archive solution: model 3921, ecliptic pole (96°, 11°)
entries.revisitWhen: Published model-specific definitions, an independently constrained pole/scale, or a released replacement mesh that resolves the recorded ambiguity.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: Shown rotation "21.2689 hours" (damit-models) differs from the LCDB V4.0 summary record 4413 period 38.41 h (U 3, synodic); the shown value is kept.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
